newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil BNDES infrastructure funding to rise in 97.
newsitem.headline: Brazil BNDES infrastructure funding to rise in 97.

text.p: Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) should approve financing of more than five billion reais ($4.81 billion) in 1997 for infrastructure projects, according to the head of the BNDES infrastructure department.

This figure compares with 3.46 billion reais ($3.33 billion) approved until the end of November this year for projects worth 8.02 billion reais ($7.71 billion), a 412 percent rise from last year's 675 million reais ($649 million) approved funding for infrastructure projects.
Fernando Perrone said BNDES financing in infrastructure was being stimulated by privatizations in the electricity, telecommunications and railway sector.

Perrone said at least 2.396 billion reais ($2.3 billion) in infrastructure funds would be disbursed in 1997, but the figure was likely to be much higher. This year the BNDES has disbursed 1.26 billion reais ($1.21 billion) in funds, up 35 percent from 1995's 932 million reais ($896.2 million).
The infrastructure projects receiving BNDES financing include the Bolivia-Brazil gas pipeline, the Ita and Salto Caxias hydroelectric plants and the port of Sepetiba among others.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
